definitions.explanation: Describing physical pain or discomfort in a part of the body.
Can also describe emotional pain or embarrassment (slang: cringe).

examples.english: I have a headache. (My head hurts.)

examples.japanese: {足|あし}が{痛|いた}くて{歩|ある}けない。
examples.english: My leg hurts so much I can't walk.

examples.japanese: ここを{押|お}すと{痛|いた}いですか。
examples.english: Does it hurt when I press here?
examples.notes: Common question at a doctor's office

examples.japanese: {昨日|きのう}{転|ころ}んで{膝|ひざ}を{打|う}ってしまいました。まだ{少|すこ}し{痛|いた}いです。
examples.english: I fell and hit my knee yesterday. It still hurts a bit.

examples.japanese: {歯|は}が{痛|いた}いので、{歯医者|はいしゃ}に{行|い}きます。
examples.english: My tooth hurts, so I'm going to the dentist.

examples.japanese: あの{言葉|ことば}は{痛|いた}い。
{友達|ともだち}にひどいことを{言|い}われて{痛|いた}かった。
examples.english: It was painful being told something terrible by a friend.

examples.japanese: {別|わか}れはいつも{痛|いた}いものだ。
お{金|かね}をたくさん{使|つか}ってしまって、{財布|さいふ}に{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: I spent so much money — it hurts my wallet.

examples.japanese: {大切|たいせつ}な{人|ひと}がいなくなるのは、{本当|ほんとう}に{痛|いた}いことだと{思|おも}います。
examples.english: I think losing someone important is truly painful.

notes:
{痛|いた}い is an i-adjective meaning painful or sore.

FORMS:
- {痛|いた}くない: not painful
- {痛|いた}くて: and it hurts...
- {痛|いた}かった: was painful

COMMON PATTERN:
Body part + が + {痛|いた}い:
- {頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}い: I have a headache
- お{腹|なか}が{痛|いた}い: my stomach hurts
- {歯|は}が{痛|いた}い: my tooth hurts

RELATED WORDS:
- {痛|いた}み: pain (noun)
- {痛|いた}める: to hurt, to injure
- {痛|いた}がる: to show signs of pain

FIGURATIVE USE:
Can describe emotional pain: {心|こころ}が{痛|いた}い (my heart aches).
